tldr.label: Key takeaways
tldr.lead: Chrome's built-in Live Caption works with headphones, because it captions the audio Chrome itself plays, without a microphone. What fails with headphones are tools that listen through the mic, including LessonScriptor's free mode. LessonScriptor's AI mode captures tab audio and works with any headphones.
bullets: Chrome's Live Caption processes audio played in the browser on-device: wired, Bluetooth, AirPods or USB headsets make no difference.

If captions vanish with headphones, the cause is elsewhere: audio playing outside Chrome (Zoom or Teams desktop app), a muted tab, a Bluetooth reconnect interrupting playback, or an incomplete speech model.
Mic-based tools (dictation, browser speech recognition, LessonScriptor's free mode) hear nothing when the sound goes into your headphones.
LessonScriptor's AI mode captures the tab's audio directly: it works with headphones and keeps an editable, exportable transcript. 30-minute free trial.
On Windows 11 (22H2+), system-wide Live Captions (Win+Ctrl+L) caption all PC audio, headphones included. Windows 10 doesn't have it.

intro: Chrome's built-in live captions work with headphones: Live Caption captions the audio Chrome itself plays, processed on-device, without going through the microphone. Plugging in AirPods, Sony WH-1000XM5s or wired headphones doesn't turn captions off. The confusion comes from elsewhere: many transcription tools listen through the microphone, and those stop hearing anything once the sound goes into your headphones. LessonScriptor's free mode is one of them. This guide explains what works with headphones, what doesn't, and how to transcribe a lecture on Moodle or a YouTube video with headphones using LessonScriptor's AI mode.

sections.h2: Do Chrome's live captions work with headphones?
sections.body:
Yes. Chrome's Live Caption captions the audio playing in browser tabs, inside Chrome, before it's sent to your speakers or headphones. Google says all audio and captions are processed locally and never leave your device. The microphone isn't involved.

So wired headphones, AirPods, Bluetooth headphones or a USB headset have no effect on captions. You can even follow a lecture with no speakers at all, which is one of the use cases Google designed the feature for.

If captions disappear when you put your headphones on, look for another cause: the lecture is running in the Zoom or Teams desktop app rather than in Chrome, the tab is muted, a Bluetooth reconnect interrupted playback, or the speech model is incomplete. Our troubleshooting guide covers all eight known causes.

sections.h2: Do Chrome live captions work with AirPods on a Mac?
sections.body:
Yes. On macOS, as on Windows, Chrome's Live Caption works with AirPods and any other headphones, because it doesn't depend on the audio output device.

If captions stop after you connect AirPods, check three things: that the video is actually playing in Chrome, that **Live Caption** is still on in **chrome://settings/accessibility**, and that Chrome was fully relaunched (Cmd+Q) after the last macOS or Chrome update. Disconnecting and reconnecting Bluetooth sometimes restarts playback.

The real headphone problem on a Mac affects tools that listen through the MacBook's microphone: once the sound goes into your AirPods, the mic can no longer hear the video.

sections.h2: What is tab audio capture and why does it work with headphones?
sections.body:
Tab audio capture is a Chrome API that lets an extension receive the audio stream of a specific browser tab, regardless of the output device.

LessonScriptor's AI mode uses tab audio capture: it receives the tab's sound before it reaches your headphones, sends it in chunks (10 seconds in Normal mode, 30 seconds in the more accurate Optimal mode) to a Whisper-class AI transcription model, and shows the text in the side panel with a short delay. The sound keeps playing in your headphones as usual.

The pipeline depends on neither the microphone nor the output device: AirPods, Sony WH-1000XM5, Bose, a USB headset or wired headphones give the same result. Each tab is independent, so you can transcribe several videos at once.

sections.h2: Is there a free headphone-friendly caption option on Windows?
sections.body:
Yes. Besides Chrome's own Live Caption, Windows 11 (version 22H2 and later) includes system-wide **Live Captions** that caption all PC audio, headphones included, not just Chrome. That helps for lectures in the Zoom or Teams desktop app.

**How to enable it on Windows 11:** press **Win+Ctrl+L**, or go to Settings > Accessibility > Captions. A caption bar appears above your windows. Several languages are available, including English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Chinese.

**Windows 10:** this feature isn't available; use Chrome's Live Caption instead.

**Limitation:** like Chrome's captions, Windows Live Captions are read-only (no editing or export), and the bar can cover part of the video. For study sessions where you need to annotate and export notes, a transcript you can keep is more useful.

sections.h2: How do I set up LessonScriptor to work with headphones?
sections.body:
Using LessonScriptor with headphones requires AI mode, because free mode listens through the microphone.

1. Install LessonScriptor from the Chrome Web Store.
2. Open your video in Chrome (a lecture on Moodle or Canvas, YouTube, Zoom in the browser) and click the LessonScriptor icon to open the side panel.
3. Choose **AI mode**. The first 30 minutes are free; after that, buy a pack if you need one.
4. Play the video: the transcript appears in the panel with a delay of a few seconds.

AI mode uses one-time packs with no subscription, consumed second by second, and credits never expire: 5h for $5, 15h for $12, 30h for $21 (Stripe shows a local-currency estimate). If you prefer free mode, use speakers at 80% volume or higher, without headphones.

sections.h2: Which headphones work with Chrome live captions?
sections.body: All headphones work with Chrome's Live Caption and with LessonScriptor's AI mode, because neither uses the microphone. Only mic-based tools need speakers.

items.q: Do Chrome live captions work with headphones?
items.a: Yes. Chrome captions the audio it plays itself, on-device, without using the microphone. Wired, Bluetooth or USB headphones don't stop captions. If they disappear, check that the video is playing in Chrome and that the tab isn't muted.

items.q: Do Chrome live captions work with AirPods?
items.a: Yes, on Mac and Windows. Live Caption doesn't depend on the audio output device. What fails with AirPods are tools that listen through the microphone, such as LessonScriptor's free mode.

items.q: Why does my transcription stop working when I wear headphones?
items.a: Your tool probably listens through the microphone. When the sound goes into your headphones, the mic can't hear the video. Use a tool that captures tab audio, such as LessonScriptor's AI mode, or use speakers.

items.q: How do I transcribe a Moodle lecture with headphones?
items.a: Open the lecture in Chrome, start LessonScriptor in AI mode and play the video. AI mode captures tab audio, so headphones don't matter, and you get an editable transcript you can export as .txt or .md.

items.q: Does Windows 10 have Live Captions like Windows 11?
items.a: No. System-wide Live Captions (Win+Ctrl+L) are only in Windows 11 version 22H2 and later. On Windows 10, use Chrome's Live Caption, which works with headphones, or LessonScriptor's AI mode.

summary.heading: Chrome live captions with headphones: the short answer
summary.body: Chrome's Live Caption works with all headphones, because it captions audio played in Chrome, on-device, without a microphone. If captions vanish with headphones, the problem is elsewhere: audio outside Chrome, a muted tab or an incomplete speech model. What fails with headphones are mic-based tools, including LessonScriptor's free mode. For a transcript you can keep, highlight and export while listening on headphones, LessonScriptor's AI mode captures tab audio and works with AirPods, Bluetooth, wired or USB headphones. On Windows 11, system-wide Live Captions are a free, read-only alternative.
